standard_prerequisites.name: The inverse system of powers of an ideal is pro-isomorphic to the system generated by the n-th powers of any finite generating set
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the system of powers by the system generated by the powers of the chosen generators, matching the situation.

standard_prerequisites.name: If an inverse system of distinguished triangles has pro-zero cones then the two outer systems are pro-isomorphic
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to showing that the system of cones is pro-zero.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a bounded inverse system of complexes it suffices to check that the cohomology systems are pro-zero, and the vanishing of those systems was established in the earlier Koszul discussion using Noetherianity
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the pro-zero property of the cones and hence finishes the proof.

core_obligations: Record the elementary pro-isomorphism between the inverse system of powers of the ideal and the inverse system generated by the powers of the chosen generators (proof lines 29654-29656).

Consider the inverse system of distinguished triangles relating the Koszul complexes of the situation to the system of powers of the generators, with the cone of the first arrow as the third term, and reduce the statement to showing that the system of cones is pro-zero (proof lines 29656-29664).

Observe that the Koszul complex has nonzero terms only in degrees from minus r plus one to zero, so the cone is bounded in an analogous way, and that its cohomology vanishes in nonnegative degrees and agrees with the Koszul cohomology in negative degrees (proof lines 29664-29671).

Conclude by the earlier computation that those cohomology systems are pro-zero, which is precisely where the Noetherian hypothesis enters, and hence that the cones are pro-zero and the statement holds (proof lines 29671-29673).
proof_roadmap: Replace the system of powers by the system generated by the powers of the generators (proof lines 29654-29656).
Reduce through the system of distinguished triangles to pro-zero-ness of the cones (proof lines 29656-29664).
Use boundedness and the earlier pro-zero computation of the Koszul cohomology to conclude (proof lines 29664-29673).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that in the Koszul setup of the section, over a Noetherian ring, the inverse system of powers of the ideal is pro-isomorphic to the inverse system of Koszul complexes, as objects of the derived category (statement lines 29647-29652, formulated inside the situation of the section). The proof replaces the powers by the system generated by the powers of the chosen generators, forms the inverse system of distinguished triangles with the cone of the comparison, and reduces to pro-zero-ness of the cones: the cones are bounded because the Koszul complex sits between degrees minus r plus one and zero, their cohomology vanishes in nonnegative degrees and agrees with the Koszul cohomology below, and the pro-zero property of the latter was established earlier, which is where the Noetherian hypothesis is used (proof lines 29654-29673). The reduction to a statement about cones is what makes the argument short. The counted statement depends on the situation of the section, which is delivered as the context span, and refers three times to earlier results, which are carried as navigation stubs.
